purpose: Public technical and admission documentation, not T1/T2/T3 performance evidence
retrieval_method: Public web page text retrieval; no account access or paid services

sources.title: Running a Relayer
facts: The V3 guide specifies a dual-core 2+ GHz CPU, 4 GB RAM and a UNIX-like OS.
Relayers need token inventory and RPC access; inventory management includes rebalancing and repayment-chain selection.
The guide describes root-bundle publication at a minimum interval of about 1.5 hours.
caveats: The page announces an upcoming protocol upgrade and API documentation.
Bundle publication interval is not a measured refund latency or an upper bound on capital lock.
Do not execute the live signing or submission instructions in this research.

sources.title: Relayer Nomination
facts: An exclusiveRelayer may alone fill a deposit until exclusivityDeadline; open filling follows expiration.
Nomination requires application and a track record including step-in fills and sub-10-second open-flow fills.
The page says most frontend flow has nominated relayers.
caveats: The implementation text refers to a Q1-Q2 2025 rollout; this is not a fresh 2026 on-chain census.
No admission, allocation, fill share or profitable open residual flow has been established for this entrant.

sources.title: Intent Lifecycle in Across
facts: The relayer fronts destination tokens, then waits for fill validation, bundle proposal, challenge and cross-chain execution before refund.
Repayment chain affects the liquidity-provider fee.
The documented bundle proposal cadence is about 1.5 hours minimum.
caveats: The documented V3 lifecycle is not verification of the latest deployed V4 behavior.
End-to-end fill-to-refund distributions must be measured rather than inferred from cadence.

sources.title: Fillers Overview
facts: Quoters are permissioned and vetted; non-exclusive fillers are permissionless.
Open filling occurs after exclusivity expires or under the specified override/missing-exclusivity conditions.
The orders API is cached, returns at most the last 50 orders, and permits at most 4 requests per second.
The retrieved guide describes RFQ plus exclusive Dutch auctions on supported chains.
caveats: Open endpoint access does not confer exclusive quoting rights.
A capped cached snapshot cannot establish the entire eligible flow or prove winning execution.

sources.title: Setting up a bonding pool
facts: An independent pool is documented with $500,000 stablecoins plus 1,500,000 COW.
An approved reduced pool starts with $50,000 stablecoins or ETH plus 500,000 COW, rising to $100,000 plus 1,000,000 COW over the following year.
Reduced pools require core-team approval and remain within the CoW DAO bonding arrangement.
caveats: These are specific self-funded pool routes, not a universal minimum cash requirement for every solver.
Do not price COW or assert a dollar bond cost without a time-aligned token quote.

sources.title: Joining The CoW Protocol Solver Competition
facts: The DAO-backed route describes company/shareholder KYC, shadow testing, onboarding and staging before production.
The current guide says DAO-backed solvers start on BNB Chain, with later L2 and mainnet evaluation.
The guide describes a 15% weekly COW-reward service fee beginning after six months.
The onboarding call covers locking 25% of weekly rewards.
Network-fee reimbursements and COW rewards are paid weekly; orderbook API access can be whitelisted.
caveats: A subsidized or delegated bond is possible in principle but no accepted admission or exception is established.
BNB-first onboarding needs explicit scope treatment: distinguish solver operations from builder-dominated arbitrage rather than silently treating the exclusion as settled.
Weekly reimbursement is not immediate liquid operating capital.

sources.title: Terms of Use for Resolvers
facts: Whitelisting eligibility requires delegation of at least 5% of total Unicorn Power, with at most 10 listed resolvers.
A permissioned-proxy collaboration route is described.
Exclusive API service levels include a 500 ms quote response and 90% fill rate over a rolling 7 calendar days.
Fusion+ includes additional native-token safety deposits.
caveats: The retrieved governance terms state last update 2025-06-16 and effective date 2025-06-17.
Legacy context only: newer 2025-11-24 and 2026-08-14 business-portal PDFs were subsequently retrieved; use ONEINCH_CURRENT for the current threshold discussion.
The 500 ms and 90% SLA figures are legacy-document facts, not asserted as verified current requirements.
No delegation agreement, proxy fee, safety-deposit schedule or accepted access exists for the entrant.
The 5% threshold is not a known USD bond price.

sources.title: 1inch Network Terms of Use for Resolvers, August 2026
facts: The PDF states last updated 2026-08-14 and effective 2026-08-15.
The retrieved whitelisting section retains a delegation threshold of at least 5% of total Unicorn Power and at most 10 listed resolvers.
The text describes permissioned proxies where applicable and enabled, rather than guaranteeing their availability.
Exclusive Resolver API selection is vetted.
caveats: The page extraction was truncated at 50000 characters; only the relevant admission and threshold sections were inspected.
Current SLA timing figures and all legal terms were not independently verified.
No accepted access, delegation price or proxy commercial agreement is established.

sources.title: Funding
facts: Funding is exchanged hourly between position holders, and its sign depends on the premium component.
The payment uses position size, oracle price and the actual interval funding rate.
caveats: The documented interest component is not a guaranteed realized funding return.
Historical, signed funding payments and hedge costs are required.

sources.title: Fees
facts: Base tier-0 validator-operated perps show 0.045% taker and 0.015% maker fees.
Base tier-0 spot shows 0.070% taker and 0.040% maker fees.
Fee tiers depend on rolling 14-day weighted volume; staking, aligned quotes and special-market rules can modify the base schedule.
caveats: Do not assign incumbent volume discounts or staking discounts to a new entrant.
Separate maker and taker fills; a limit order is not evidence of a maker fill.

sources.title: Rate limits and user limits
facts: REST requests share an aggregate weight allowance of 1200 per minute per IP; requests have method-specific weights.
The public EVM JSON-RPC endpoint is documented at 100 requests per minute.
Address action and high-congestion allowances depend on trading history and maker activity.
caveats: Rate allowance is not a latency or execution-quality guarantee.
Read-only information limits and signed-action limits differ.

sources.title: Rate Limits
facts: The MEV-Share guide lists 1800 bundle submissions and 300 bundle simulations per minute per IP for the named methods.
caveats: Other Flashbots API pages describe different method scopes and limits; do not mix them.
Do not send bundles or signed transactions during this study.

sources.title: Bundle Inclusion Troubleshooting
facts: A bundle may not be included because of reversion, insufficient incentive, higher competing bids, late receipt or validator configuration.
Simulation success alone does not establish inclusion.
caveats: Builder-bid, refund and timing effects must be evaluated using the relevant auction.
The source's live submission and signing procedures are out of scope.

sources.title: Alchemy Pricing: Free, Pay as You Go & Enterprise Plans
facts: The free plan lists 30 million compute units monthly and 15 requests per second.
The pay-as-you-go compute rate is $0.52 per million compute units.
The retrieved page lists 300 RPS/10000 CU per second included pay-as-you-go throughput, with additional capacity priced separately.
caveats: This is a public price schedule, not a bill, account entitlement, spending authorization or latency measurement.
Method weights, archive methods, traces, peak throughput, storage, redundancy and servers affect actual cost.

sources.title: Bots and Automations
facts: The page lists maintained Blue and Midnight liquidators, community Rust and Go liquidators, and vault reallocation tooling.
The Blue bot discovers borrowers, reads current chain state and simulates before submission.
caveats: Open source bot availability is evidence against assuming an unserved niche, not an on-chain count of active profitable competitors.
Protocol TVL is not proof every listed market/version satisfies this study's age, audit and liquidity gates.

sources.title: FAQ
facts: PT can redeem the underlying yield-bearing token after maturity; YT no longer accrues after maturity.
The page warns about risks in third-party protocols and their contracts.
caveats: Principal in underlying units is not a risk-free USD redemption.
Selling before maturity requires executable market prices and costs.
Underlying protocol, issuer, bridge and chain exposures remain common failure domains.

sources.title: Automation Architecture
facts: The Automation Registry governs nodes and compensates successful upkeep execution.
The page describes both developer upkeep registration and node-operator participation.
caveats: Developer job registration is not proof of an entrant's admission to compensated node rotation.
No accepted node status, accessible bounty backlog, operator PnL or onboarding terms were measured.

sources.title: Concentrated Liquidity
facts: Liquidity outside its chosen price interval becomes inactive and earns no fees.
As price moves toward a boundary, the position can become entirely one asset.
Multiple positions do not remove the underlying pool/protocol/asset exposures.
caveats: Fee growth is not net LP profit.
Active-liquidity share, inventory marks, hedge costs and executable exits must be replayed.
